title: Emberwell Brew House menu-card set: neutralize a mixed-light café food/drink batch to an in-frame grey card, author one warm house look, deepen a signature cooler to a seasonal colorway, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge one press-ready card per menu item

source.reference: Menu design for a neighborhood brew cafe

grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Upwork café-menu brief (a neighborhood brew café wanting a designer with 'Proficiency in Adobe InDesign' and a 'Strong sense of typography, layout, and print design' to deliver a full food-and-drinks menu, print-ready files, and editable InDesign source, in a 'warm, cozy, and elevated' style). Real client/persona laundered to the FICTIONAL 'Emberwell Brew House' — no real company, person, product, or trademark is named (the prior draft's 'Hearthstone' collided with a real card-game trademark and is replaced). REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the raw brief implies a single from-scratch menu laid out by hand, which is NOT connector scope (nothing composes a free-form layout), and a single all-items-on-one-page menu cannot be produced by a data-merge — document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW and cannot place many records on one page, and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields. So the deliverable is modeled as what the merge genuinely produces and what a café genuinely uses: a set of printed MENU FEATURE CARDS (one single-record counter/table card per menu item) that together form the menu. The client supplies a hand-authored single-record InDesign card template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> and THREE @-prefixed image-path columns (one for the item's dish photo, one for the shared masthead wordmark, one for the shared kraft background texture), the menu roster as a CSV, a batch of raw café food/drink captures shot across a service window under mismatched café light — each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame — and a flat wordmark on warm off-white paper. The Adobe chain then does the real, rewarded work: neutralize every capture to its own in-frame grey card so the whole set shares one white point, carry one authored warm house look across all of them without wrecking any dish's genuine color, deepen the bright-red hibiscus cooler to a seasonal spiced-cranberry colorway without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark for a crisp masthead, license the kraft/linen background from Adobe Stock, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready PDF (one card per item) plus a high-resolution JPEG set for the café's social and delivery-app listings.
one_line_ask: Bring a batch of mixed-light café food and drink captures to one warm, appetizing house look by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries, keep every dish's true color under the grade, deepen the signature cooler to a seasonal colorway without reshooting, prep and vectorize the café wordmark, license a kraft background, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign card template against the menu roster to produce a press-ready card per item plus a high-res JPEG set.
full_brief:
Emberwell Brew House is a warm neighborhood café refreshing its menu for the counter and the tables. Rather than one crowded sheet, we print the menu as a set of small feature cards — one card per item — that sit in the holders by the register and on the tables, and the same set doubles as our posts and delivery-app photos. We have the card template built and the copy written; what we need is the imagery brought up to standard and the cards produced.

Here is the problem with the photos. Our staff shot the food and drinks over one busy morning in whatever spot was free — some by the cool front window, some under the warm pendant lamps over the bar, a couple in the dim back corner, one or two out on the sunny patio — so straight out of the folder they are a mismatched jumble: some cool and blue, some warm and amber, one or two underexposed, one blown out and hot, and several sitting at a slight tilt. A set of cards that don't match reads cheap. Because we knew the light was a mess, whoever shot them clipped a small neutral grey card into the corner of every frame. Your job on the imagery: bring the whole batch to ONE deliberately warm, cozy, appetizing look by neutralizing each capture against the grey card it carries — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point. Then carry a single house look across all of them: a warm, morning-light feel — gently warm highlights, clean neutral shadows, a little contrast and clarity, a restrained vibrance lift — so every card feels like it came from the same shoot. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each capture was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure, and tone decision to land on the shared look. And be careful with the dishes that are supposed to be a strong color — the butter croissant is genuinely deep golden and one of the drinks is a true bright red; if a dish's grey card already reads neutral, do not 'correct' a cast that isn't there, and do not let the warm grade drag our green plates (the avocado toast, the matcha) toward a dull olive. When you're done, tell us the white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm they were matched, not eyeballed. Second, a seasonal card without a reshoot: our signature iced cooler is a bright hibiscus red today — give us a deeper, spiced-cranberry / mulled version of that same shot for the seasonal card (a rich, dark berry-red in the SAME family, just deepened and slightly muted, not a jump to a new hue), and the new color has to sit under the real highlights, ice and shadow of the drink, not as a flat dead fill or a wash over the whole glass and table. Third, our wordmark only exists as a flat piece on warm off-white paper, slightly crooked — get it clean and razor-sharp as a vector so it sits crisp at the top of every card and scales to the A-frame board. Fourth, back the cards with a warm kraft / linen texture — source one you like. Finally, build the cards: we have hand-built the InDesign card template with the real placeholder fields and the image slots, and we're giving you the roster; merge them so every menu item gets its own single-page card with its copy bound, its matching graded photo dropped in, the crisp wordmark at the masthead and the kraft behind it, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI card per item plus a high-resolution JPEG set for social and the delivery apps. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our descriptions or prices. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole batch matched to one warm white point with each dish's true color intact; the cooler recolor natural under its own light; the wordmark a clean skew-free vector; and exactly one finished card per roster row.

inputs.name: emberwell_card_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A6-portrait (approx 105x148mm) café menu feature card — ONE item per page — in a warm, cozy, elevated style with clean humanist/serif type and generous margins. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<tagline>>, <<item>>, <<desc>>, <<price>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate frames: a hero dish-photo frame at a 4:5 ratio bound to @image, a LIGHT CREAM masthead panel at the top bound to @Wordmark (so the vectorized wordmark sits on a light panel, not on the mid-tone kraft — its enclosed letter counters, which knock out to white through the vectorize path, read correctly against cream), and a full-bleed background frame bound to @Texture for the kraft/linen. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark and the texture reach the card ONLY as merge binds through their image columns — never dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so all merge fields and all three image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record feature card is the correct, connector-doable shape (a single all-items menu page cannot be data-merged). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would NOT bind (this is the merge trap). THREE image columns (@image, @Wordmark, @Texture) mean the merge resolves the row's graded dish photo plus the shared vectorized wordmark and the shared kraft texture per card, giving the chain-produced wordmark and the licensed texture a connector-doable path onto every card without any free-form placement (mirrors the two-image-column merge pattern used in the passing line-sheet exemplar). The masthead panel is authored as a light cream field precisely so the vectorized wordmark's white-filled counters read correctly and no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

inputs.name: emberwell_menu_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns tagline,item,desc,price,@image,@Wordmark,@Texture holding 10 café menu rows, one per feature card: (Breakfast) Buttermilk Pancake Stack; (Breakfast) Farmhouse Avocado Toast; (All-Day) Cortado; (Coffee & Tea) Emberwell Flat White; (Coffee & Tea) Ceremonial Matcha Latte; (Coffee & Tea) Salted Iced Mocha; (Pastry) Butter Croissant; (Pastry) Wild Blueberry Muffin; (All-Day) Hibiscus Cooler; (Seasonal) Spiced Cranberry Cooler. Each row carries a short, warm one-line description (<<desc>>), a US-dollar price (<<price>>, e.g. $5.50), and a short section eyebrow (<<tagline>>, e.g. 'Breakfast'). The @image column names the matching prepped photo file the agent produces (e.g. @flatwhite_card.jpg for the Flat White row, and @seasonal_card.jpg for the Spiced Cranberry Cooler row, which uses the recolored cooler variant). The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @emberwell_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row. The @Texture column holds the SAME licensed kraft file — @kraft_linen_texture.jpg — in EVERY row. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<tagline>>,<<item>>,<<desc>>,<<price>> and the three @image-path columns @image,@Wordmark,@Texture.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplies the real menu copy the brief calls for; headers match the authored .indd fields and all three @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct per-item photo, the shared wordmark, and the shared kraft per card. @Wordmark and @Texture carry identical shared paths in all ten rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark SVG and the licensed texture a connector-doable path onto every card via the merge (not free-form placement). Ten rows => the merge must produce exactly ten finished cards. The @image column names AGENT-PRODUCED outputs the agent names per its own triage of the neutral raw captures — nothing in this file tells the agent which raw capture is which dish, which is cool or warm, or which one is the already-neutral trap; the roster states the item copy and the target filename convention only, never a treatment.

inputs.name: raw_menu_captures_x9.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 9 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless café food-and-drink captures, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, before any crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, and each shot over one busy morning under mismatched café light. Contents and conditions: (01) a flat white coffee in a ceramic cup with latte-art fern on a marble counter, cool front-window light with a bluish cast, frame tilted ~3 deg, a blurred pastry case behind; (02) a tall stack of buttermilk pancakes with butter and syrup on a white plate on a wood table, warm pendant-lamp light, slightly UNDER-exposed and dull, level, cluttered salt-shaker background; (03) an avocado toast plate with radish, chili and a poached egg on sourdough, cool north-window light with a blue cast, frame tilted ~4 deg, cutlery clutter — the sliced avocado and herbs are a genuine fresh green; (04) a deep golden butter croissant on a small plate beside a linen napkin, shot in near-neutral light so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral (the warmth is the real baked color, not a white-balance error), level; (05) a cortado in a small clear glass on a saucer on a marble counter, old GREEN-ish shop fluorescent light, level, blurred espresso machine behind; (06) a wild-blueberry muffin on a plate, warm tungsten lamp, amber cast, frame tilted ~3 deg; (07) a tall iced HIBISCUS cooler that is a genuine BRIGHT RED in a clear glass with ice and a citrus wheel, mixed window+lamp light, level (this is the hero for the seasonal recolor); (08) a ceremonial matcha latte with a bright true-green foam layer in a glass, flat and clearly UNDER-exposed, level; (09) a salted iced mocha in a tall glass, clearly OVER-exposed and warm (blown highlights on the ice, hot cast), level. Every shot has real crumb/glaze/ice/fabric texture, cluttered café-counter surroundings, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each frame; the captures are delivered as a zip of 9 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs named raw_menu_captures_x9.zip#01 .. #09.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each 4:5 card crop fills the template's hero frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure and tilt vary) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own reasoned decision toward one shared warm white point, and the agent neutralizes each in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE (never reading a pixel/channel value) and REPORTS the parameters it dialed. THE TRAP FRAMES: #04 (butter croissant) is genuinely deep golden and was shot under neutral light, so its card is ALREADY neutral — the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set); a naive agent that batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' correction, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real baked color. #03 (avocado) and #08 (matcha) carry genuine greens that the shared warm grade will drag toward olive unless their green hue is protected. #07 (hibiscus) carries the genuine bright red for the masked recolor branch. #02 (under-exposed, warm) and #09 (over-exposed, warm) demand OPPOSITE tonal moves. Filenames are a NEUTRAL #01..#09 scheme so the agent must open each to decide its treatment — nothing in the filename telegraphs the lighting, the tilt, or which frame is the trap.

inputs.name: emberwell_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop capture of the 'Emberwell Brew House' wordmark inked on warm off-white textured paper: an elegant condensed serif in deep espresso-brown with a small coffee-bean glyph, generous open letter counters. Rendered as a real paper piece — the ground is a warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the surface, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplied as a flat mark on warm off-white paper, slightly rotated, with margin and soft edges — so image_vectorize would trace the paper field and the skew if fed raw, forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast and drop the off-white ground toward white, crop to the mark's bounds, knock the ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. The serif is drawn with OPEN counters and the template masthead is a light cream panel, so the vectorized mark's white-filled counters (a known image_remove_background→vectorize behavior) read correctly — no dark-ground knockout is claimed. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering. Filename states the asset only; the scan-nature/skew that drives the prep chain lives in this note, not the filename.

outputs.name: Emberwell_MenuCards_print.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly ten press-ready A6-portrait (approx 105x148mm) menu feature cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 10) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its tagline/item/desc/price verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized 4:5 photo dropped into the hero frame (via @image), the vectorized wordmark dropped into the light cream masthead (via @Wordmark) and the licensed kraft texture into the full-bleed background (via @Texture) — all by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality at card trim, with bleed. The Spiced Cranberry Cooler seasonal card (its @image is the recolored cooler variant) is simply one page of this set, not a separately exported file.

outputs.name: Emberwell_MenuCards_highres.jpg
outputs.spec: High-resolution JPEG export of the same merged card set (the whole merged document rendered to max-quality JPEG, one image per card) for the café's social feeds and delivery-app listings. Exported by document_render_layout from the same merged document as the PDF — not a per-record pull.

outputs.name: graded_menu_photos_x9
outputs.spec: Nine grey-card-neutralized, straightened café photos carried to one warm house look, delivered as the 4:5 card crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the cards, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one shared warm white point, each dish's genuine color intact (the golden croissant not cooled, the greens not dragged to olive); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 4:5 card crop (grey card fully cropped OUT, no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-cropped-out product crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: variant_cooler_spiced_cranberry.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored seasonal variant of the hibiscus cooler hero: the bright hibiscus red deepened to a spiced-cranberry / mulled berry-red via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red — an in-band adjacent shift, no near-complementary rotation) riding the drink's existing luminosity, so its ice highlights, surface sheen and cast shadow stay natural and the glass, citrus wheel and table are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill. Cropped to the same 4:5 card frame; binds into the Spiced Cranberry Cooler seasonal card via @image.

outputs.name: emberwell_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the wordmark, traced only after the paper piece is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead and A-frame-board scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Reaches every card through the @Wordmark merge column and sits on the template's light cream masthead panel so the open, white-filled counters read correctly.

connector_workflow.note: Search Adobe Stock for a warm kraft-paper / linen texture to back the cards and reinforce the cozy feel (low-res candidates). The chosen texture becomes the shared @Texture background bound onto every card by the merge.

License and download the chosen kraft/linen texture at full-res (license BEFORE use). Uploaded under the exact name the roster's @Texture column references so the merge resolves it as the shared full-bleed background.
Triage: capture 01 is tilted ~3 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted captures get straightened — deciding which is part of the job; the level frames skip this.) REPORT the correcting angle.

Cool bluish front-window cast: WARM the temperature and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral BY EYE, then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey — and in the SAME call lay the shared authored house look as constants: gently warm highlights, clean neutral shadows, modest contrast + clarity, a restrained vibrance lift. The WB/exposure are reasoned to THIS frame's cast; the house-look tonal shape is the batch-wide constant. This is an agent-authored split-tone from primitives — NOT a preset, NOT auto-tone. Report the temperature/tint/exposure move. Replaces the deprecated color_temperature / vibrance_and_saturation / dark_portions tools.

Crop the neutralized frame to the 4:5 hero ratio the card template expects, framing on the cup with the grey card cropped OUT — this crop binds into the Flat White card. The pre-crop neutralized master (flatwhite_neutral, grey card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop, and card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4000-4500 px source, never enlarging.

Capture 02 (warm pendant light, level, slightly UNDER-exposed): the dominant move is tonal — LIFT exposure and add a touch of contrast/clarity — then cool the mild warm cast so its grey card reads neutral and matches the shared white point. Lay the same house-look constants. Distinct numbers from frame 1 because the light differed. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Capture 03 is tilted ~4 deg — level it. REPORT the angle (different from frame 1).

Cool north-window cast: warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, set exposure to match set brightness, lay the house-look constants. Report the move. (The genuine avocado green is protected in the next masked step so the warm grade doesn't drag it to olive.)

Semantically select 'the sliced avocado and green herbs on the toast' — a real object, not a hue or coordinate region — returning a maskURI so the green can be held true without touching the rest of the plate.

Masked hue-protection (consumes the neutralized frame + the green mask): inside the mask, hold the green band's hue and restore the saturation/luminance the warm house grade pulled out, so the avocado reads as fresh green rather than olive. image_adjust_hsl is the only masked recolor path; this is a small in-band correction, not a rotation. This masked output is the retained neutralized master (grey card still in frame).
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. Capture 04's butter croissant is genuinely deep golden and was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set and lay the house-look constants. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move used on frames 1/3, or that 'cools an imagined blue cast', will push this card off-neutral and strip the real baked color. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Capture 05 (green-ish shop fluorescent, level): neutralize with a TINT (green->magenta) correction as well as a temperature nudge until its grey card reads neutral to the shared white point — a different axis from the warm/cool frames; a temperature-only fix leaves the card green. Lay the house-look constants. Report the tint magnitude.
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Capture 06 is tilted ~3 deg under warm tungsten — level it. REPORT the angle.

Capture 06 (warm amber tungsten cast): this frame must move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — COOL the temperature until its grey card reads neutral and matches the shared white point; protect the blueberry so it doesn't go magenta. Lay the house-look constants. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Capture 07, the hibiscus cooler hero (mixed window+lamp light, level): a modest neutralize to bring its grey card to the shared white point, holding the genuine bright red true. Lay the house-look constants. This neutralized full-res frame feeds BOTH the regular card crop AND the seasonal recolor branch, so keep it before cropping. Report the move.
Crop the neutralized hero to the 4:5 frame (the bright-red version that binds into the All-Day Hibiscus Cooler card). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

On the neutralized hero, semantically select only the red hibiscus drink in the glass ('the red iced hibiscus tea inside the glass') so the recolor is confined to the liquid and the glass, citrus wheel and table stay untouched. Returns a maskURI — a real object, not a hue/coordinate selection.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes hero + cooler mask): keep the drink in the red family but deepen it toward spiced cranberry — a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in red/berry; NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a luminance drop that darkens the liquid, letting the drink's existing luminosity carry the ice highlights, surface sheen and cast shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would wash the whole glass and table) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the ice and sheen) — both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the drink lands on the rich spiced-cranberry / mulled target instead of a flat brick or a still-bright candy red, still riding the original luminosity so the ice and sheen stay natural. A deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.
Crop the finished spiced-cranberry variant to the 4:5 hero frame; binds into the Seasonal Spiced Cranberry Cooler card via @image. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Capture 08 (matcha latte, flat and clearly UNDER-exposed, level): LIFT exposure and add contrast/clarity as the dominant move, then neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Lay the house-look constants. Its true green foam is protected in the next masked step. Report the move (tonal-dominant, unlike the WB-dominant frames).
Semantically select 'the green matcha foam in the glass' so its genuine green can be held true under the warm house grade without touching the milk or glass. Returns a maskURI.

Masked hue-protection: inside the mask, hold the green band's hue and restore the saturation the warm grade muted so the matcha reads vivid ceremonial green, not olive. Small in-band correction via the only masked path. This masked output is the retained neutralized master (grey card still in frame).
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Capture 09 (salted iced mocha, clearly OVER-exposed and warm, level): PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown ice, then COOL to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — the OPPOSITE tonal AND WB direction from the under-exposed warm pancakes frame, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Lay the house-look constants. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:5 hero frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Frames 01-09 now share one warm white point, each neutralized to its own grey card with its true color intact.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark sits ~2 deg rotated on the paper — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed piece to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the warm off-white paper toward white so the espresso lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast piece traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the paper margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The serif has OPEN counters and the card masthead is light cream, so the counters that fill to white through this path read correctly — no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead and the A-frame board. Tracing the raw paper piece instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. Uploaded under the name the roster's @Wordmark column references.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: flatwhite_card.jpg, pancakes_card.jpg, toast_card.jpg, croissant_card.jpg, cortado_card.jpg, muffin_card.jpg, hibiscus_card.jpg, matcha_card.jpg, mocha_card.jpg, seasonal_card.jpg, emberwell_wordmark.svg, kraft_linen_texture.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the ten 4:5 card crops (nine graded dishes + the recolored seasonal variant), the vector wordmark and the licensed kraft texture, uploaded under the exact names the roster's @image / @Wordmark / @Texture columns reference so the merge resolves each per row.

Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's three @-image columns resolve to — the per-card dish photo, the shared vectorized wordmark and the shared kraft texture — for each single-record card's hero, masthead and background frames.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the ten roster rows (tagline/item/desc/price) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve all THREE image columns per row — the row's graded photo into the @image hero frame, the vectorized wordmark (from @Wordmark, same SVG every row) into the light cream masthead, and the kraft (from @Texture, same file every row) into the full-bleed background — producing EXACTLY ONE merged card per row (ten cards). Binding the wordmark and texture through image columns is what puts them on every card: free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, so the merge is their only connector-doable path. [T] requires the hand-authored template; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would NOT bind (the merge trap), and a multi-record grid is impossible with this tool.

Export the merged single-record cards to press-ready ~300 DPI A6 PDF, one card per item. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all ten cards, one page per item) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so the seasonal card is simply one page of this set. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 10; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

Export the same merged document to a high-resolution JPEG set (one max-quality image per card) for the café's social feeds and delivery-app listings — the whole-document render, not a per-record pull.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. The kraft texture chains asset_search(1) -> asset_license_and_download_stock(2).
